subject: Acme - Integration & RSP schema follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Acme - Integration & RSP schema follow-up

Hi Alex / Emily,

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to learn about Acme's use case and requirements. Quick recap and the follow-ups we promised: 

Call recap (high level)
- You want an in-app assistant that can surface product docs, run semantic search + reranker, and optionally call back-end actions (create tickets, fetch account info).
- Latency target for the UI: median < 300ms for search + rerank responses; streaming OK for the chat assistant.
- Security: API keys stored in your Vault, rotation required.

Action items / questions for integration + schema decisions
1) SDK & auth: You mentioned Vault-managed API keys. Will you want short-lived tokens / OAuth exchange (client credentials) or simple API-key rotation?
2) Chat vs completions: Do you plan to use the assistant as a chat-style flow (multi-turn state kept client-side) or single-turn completions for each action? We recommend chat + function-calling when you need deterministic structured output.
3) Structured output / RSP schema: We should agree on a JSON schema for tool-calls and structured responses (fields, required types). I attached a draft (rsp-schema-draft.json).
4) Tokenization & max_tokens: Average user messages you mentioned were ~800 tokens peak — can you confirm typical prompt length distribution (5/50/95 percentiles)? Also, do you need hard guarantees (truncate) vs best-effort behavior?
5) Streaming semantics: We support streaming deltas. For structured tool-calling, you can stream partial content but should parse finalization events. Is your UI set up to accumulate partial tokens and render progressively?
6) Embeddings & reranker: Will you use embeddings for semantic retrieval only, or do you want an in-model reranker as well? What vector dimension/latency expectations do you have?

Next steps
- If you can share a small sample of user prompts and a sample dataset (anonymized), we can validate tokenization and provide batching/quantization recs.
- I'll loop in Dev for a short technical sync on schema + streaming behavior — propose Wed morning PT.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, rsp-schema-draft.json

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few quick answers to your questions and a couple clarifications: 

1) Auth: We use HashiCorp Vault and prefer short-lived tokens via a client-credentials exchange where our backend requests a temporary token. We can do API keys if easier, but rotation + audit is a must.

2) Chat vs completions: We'll run both patterns. Primary UI is chat (multi-turn). For certain support macros we'll do single-turn completions. For the chat assistant we want structured JSON output for downstream actions.

3) Schema: Attached is a small sample of the JSON payloads we've been capturing (acme-sample-payloads.csv). The JSON structure in rsp-schema-draft.json looks close — we'll review with engineering.

4) Tokenization: Average prompt size ~350 tokens, 95th ~1,200 tokens in extreme cases. We do want predictable truncation behavior rather than silent cutoffs.

5) Streaming: Streaming is important for perceived latency; we'd like to stream partial content in the chat and then receive the final structured object.

6) Embeddings / reranker: We'll use embeddings for initial retrieval, then a reranker to improve precision. We'd prefer a compact embedding (>= 768 dims) and sub-50ms embedding latency if possible.

Happy to join a technical sync Wed. Can Marissa loop in Dev?

—Alex

Thanks Alex — very helpful. Quick answers and what we'll bring to the tech sync: 

Auth / SDK
- We support both API-key (long-lived) and short-lived tokens. For Vault-based short-lived tokens we recommend an exchange flow: your backend exchanges a client credential for a short-lived inference token (scoped) — we can provide example code in our SDK (Node/Python).

Chat vs completions / structured output
- For deterministic JSON tool outputs we recommend the chat endpoint + function-calling (server-side) — function-calling enforces schema-like responses and reduces model hallucinations versus free-form completions.

Tokenization, max_tokens, stop sequences
- max_tokens is enforced as a response token limit. We treat it as a hard cap on generated tokens; if you need guaranteed completion of a structured object, you should size max_tokens accordingly and include stop sequences that indicate end-of-object.
- We'll run the sample payloads you shared against our tokenizer and return percentile token counts so you can size prompts and max_tokens.

Streaming semantics
- Streaming emits delta events: role/content fragments and finalization markers. For function-calls the stream will include the function name and partial args; you should accumulate until the final "finish_reason" or function-complete marker is emitted.

Embeddings & reranker
- We'll recommend a 768 or 1024-d embedding model depending on your recall/latency tradeoff. Reranking can be done via an on-model cross-attention reranker or an embedding dot-product rank + small model re-score. We'll size and bench both options.

Next steps:
- Dev, can we do a 30m call Wed 10:00 AM PT to go over schema + streaming/SDK examples?
- Alex/Emily, if you can share a small anonymized set (5-10 prompts) and indicate the 50/95 token percentiles, we'll run tokenization and return guidance.

Attaching: redwood-sdks.md excerpt (link in drive) and the draft schema again.

Best,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Acme - Integration & RSP schema follow-up

Hi Alex / Emily — looping in a few quick technical notes ahead of Wed's sync. I'll share sample request/response snippets you can paste into your integration.

1) Structured output recommendation
- Use the chat endpoint with function-calling and a concise JSON Schema. Example flow: user -> messages[] + functions[] (JSON Schema) -> model returns function call with name + arguments (JSON). Server executes and responds with the function result. Attached is rsp-schema-draft.json with an example schema for the "create_ticket" and "fetch_account" actions.

2) Tokenization & max_tokens
- Tokenization: our tokenizer is BPE-like. Rough rule-of-thumb: tokens ~ 0.75 * characters for English prose, but we will run your sample set and return exact counts.
- max_tokens: enforced per-response. If you need to guarantee complete JSON payloads, set max_tokens = expected_payload_tokens + 50 buffer and include a stop sequence such as "\n--END--" after the JSON.

3) Streaming semantics details
- Stream payloads are incremental deltas. For chat function calls: early deltas will emit "role: assistant" + partial content. The model then emits a function_call object with name + partial arguments. Continue to accumulate until you receive the final "finish_reason": "function_call" and the final args chunk.
- Implementation note: do not attempt to parse partial JSON until finish marker; instead append chunks to a buffer and validate once finished.

4) Embeddings & reranker guidance
- Embedding model: we recommend redwood-embed-1 (1024 dims) for highest recall; redwood-embed-compact (768 dims) if you need lower latency and smaller index size.
- Typical pattern: precompute embeddings for docs, do approximate k-NN (HNSW), then rerank top-K (K=50) with either a small cross-encoder or an in-model re-ranker. For cost/latency we suggest dot-product scoring + a light-weight re-ranker for the top 10.
- Batching: batch embeddings requests (128-256 inputs) to improve throughput. For online single-request embeddings we still keep p99 < 50ms for compact model under our Dedicated setup.

5) Examples / snippets (high level)
- Chat request (pseudo): messages=[{role: 'system', content: '...'}, {role:'user', content:'...'}], functions=[{name:'create_ticket', parameters: {type:'object', properties:{title:{type:'string'}, priority:{type:'string'}}}}], stream=true
- On stream: collect tokens, on finish parse function_call.arguments as JSON and execute.

I'll bring a prepared demo schema and a short Node/Python SDK snippet to Wed. If you can confirm Wed 10am PT, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
